title: A sprint worker ends every background process and monitor before it returns
goal: .claude/agents/kb-worker.md and the kb-sprint brief tell a worker to end every background command and monitor it started before returning, and land refuses a branch whose worker worktree still has a live process, naming it; a test plants a worktree with a live child process

gates.question: How does land find a live process in a worker's worktree, and what does it do where it cannot look?
options: /proc/<pid>/cwd on Linux, lsof -d cwd on other POSIX hosts, none on Windows; where it cannot look it says so and removes the clean worktree
lsof +D <path> on POSIX only; where it cannot look it refuses
ps on POSIX, PowerShell Get-CimInstance on Windows (no working directory there, so command lines only)
gates.recommendation: /proc/<pid>/cwd on Linux, lsof -d cwd on other POSIX hosts, none on Windows; where it cannot look it says so and removes the clean worktree
gates.answer: /proc/<pid>/cwd on Linux, lsof -d cwd on other POSIX hosts, none on Windows; where it cannot look it says so and removes the clean worktree

notes: SP-3brmvlnh retrospective: a worker left a ten-minute intake run with tests.py under it, and another left monitors that woke the orchestrator a dozen times.
